description: The pie chart visually represents the proportional distribution of various dialogue state tracking slots, as analyzed in the context of the paper “Continual Dialogue State Tracking via Reason-of-Select Distillation.” The chart is segmented into 16 distinct categories, each labeled with a slot name and its corresponding percentage. The largest segment is “date” at 19.30%, followed by “from” at 17.00%, “to” at 14.50%, and “genre” at 13.50%. Smaller segments include “name” (5.20%), “size” (4.20%), “intent” and “location” (both 3.80%), “destination” (3.00%), “city” (2.60%), “class” (2.40%), “range” (2.20%), “type” (2.00%), “beds” (1.30%), and “passengers” (1.10%). Each slice is color-coded and labeled with a leader line pointing to its value, with no legend provided. The segments are arranged clockwise from the top, roughly in descending order of magnitude, with the largest slices occupying the top-right quadrant and the smallest clustered near the top-left. The chart emphasizes the relative importance or frequency of each slot in the dialogue state tracking task under study.
